steps.text: Bring condensed soup, sugar, vinegar, and oil to a boil in a saucepan. Stir well, remove from the heat, and let cool until needed.
At the same time, bring a large pot of water to a boil; add carrots and boil until just tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain carrots and transfer to a mixing bowl. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery. Pour soup mixture over vegetables and stir until coated. Cover and refrigerate, 8 hours to overnight, before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Copper Pennies
raw_recipe.description: Try this old-fashioned copper pennies salad for tender carrot slices, celery, onion, and bell pepper marinated overnight in a sweetened tomato vinaigrette.

review.reviewBody: I USED HALF OF THE SUGAR,AND HALF OF THE VINEGAR,JUST RIGHT

I enjoyed this recipe as a starter/build on recipe. However, the next time I prepare it, as a matter of personal preference I would only cook the carrots a couple of minutes or not at all. For my taste the marinade was a little too sweet, I would cut the sugar or increase the vinegar. Also, I felt that a splash of worcestire and prepared mustard would have jazzed this recipe up. I enjoy things zesty and spicy so I would throw in some pepper flakes and garlic. The recipe said to chop, which to me indicates smaller pieces. The next time I will cut the peppers, onions, and celery, it will be a little closer to bite size, to equal the carrots. I might try this recipe again with some modifications.

Yummy! We love to have this salad in the fridge all summer long. One way I like to serve this is as a topping/dressing over a green salad. Topped w/ crumbled bacon makes it really excellent. I've started cutting back on the oil and never really noticed a difference. I use about 1/4C. of oil and 1/3C. vinegar. Also I switched the sugar to Splenda and decreased that to 1/3C. Love this salad!
I made mostly as written, but used 0 calorie Stevia instead of sugar and used jalapeño instead of bell pepper . It was fabulous
Substituted maple syrup for the sugar, apple cider vinegar for the white vinegar. We enjoyed it warm instead of salad-style. it was tangy and delicious. Great with steak.

I've been making this for decades (and now I'm a grandma). It's very popular! My recipe never had celery. I prefer that the onions and peppers (sliced thin, not chopped) aren't so sharp and raw, so I mix them into the hot dressing first so they wilt a little, and then add the carrots. Even better if you add a teaspoon each of mustard (dry or prepared) and Worcestershire sauce, and 1/4 tsp dried dill weed.

Outstanding! I haven't made these but once since the mid 1980s, trying to convince my memory that, YES, the tomato soup DOES work with this, haaa. So I took this along with "broccoli sizzle nuts with dates" as the added veggies to a cookout for 11 of us. Everyone liked or loved this! 2 of the 11 commented, as if puzzled by this and maybe offput by it initially, that it was "sweet". They were not expecting that. It was almost like they were waiting for an explanation, haaa. But with my comment about using an alternative sweetener, and noting that sweetness is intentional, everyone was pleased. That said, I might use less sweetener in the future. I had one deal-breaker change for our group: I substituted a Swerve brown-sugar replacement for the white sugar. Other adjustments were inconsequential for the recipe, changing the balance of flavors. First, I reached capacity on the pot I'd pulled out for carrots, at about 1.5 versus 2 pounds, so I stopped with that. Also I'd debated on omitting the 1-3 stalks* of celery since I knew one person who doesn't like celery at all. (Haaa, he lost, but ate it anyway.) Also, used less green pepper since some of our group aren't big fans of raw green pepper. Note: my final product was darker and thicker than your finished recipe as shown. (Folks would initially think it was from my subbing a brown-sweetener product, but that wasn't it, despite the obvious logic. I mention this because some younger or novice cooks want to replicate the exact look in their finished products. It's all delicious!) -Hand-sliced all of this, so pieces varied a wee bit in size, to absolutely no consequence. I did a fine dice for the celery, green pepper, and onion. The recipe, of course, is very forgiving. BTW, this was an outstanding dish to serve outdoors with our temps. in the 90s. I had chilled it overnight, but I served it unchilled. *I think the recipe lists one stalk celery, but the video showed 3 stalks laid out at some point. I'm all for adding diverse nutrition where possible, so I compromised with just two stalks.
There is way too much sugar in this recipe. A tablespoon will suffice.
I made it even easier by boiling my carrots in the tomato soup mixture. I like my carrots a little crunchy and made it a one pot side. Less dishes!
Too much sugar, use Monk fruit sweetener instead. I cook my carrots only 8 minutes!
I added a 1/2 tsp of sugar to the water because my carrots were a little bitter. I also decreased the tomato soup by about 2oz
Used to make this years ago, dug out my old recipe which is identical to this and this salad is a crowd pleaser.
This dish is absolutely delicious and will now be a permanent recipe in my house for my family. It’s outstanding.
Made it just the way it says, except might leave out the oil next time
Love it the longer it sits tge better it taste..
I never liked carrots that much, but I love this recipe
Exactly as I remember my grandmother’s recipe!
I love this recipe, I lost my recipe years ago and I'm so glad it was posted again. It was a big hit in the 70's and 80's.

I would add maybe some Worcestershire sauce. It was very good and I made half the recipe because there is only my husband and I. I like the sauce and would be good with cabbage or broccoli or cucumber and onions. The sauce would have multiple uses
